articles.title: Why these startup CEOs don’t think AI will replace human roles

articles.title: OpenAI reportedly finalizing $100B deal at more than $850B valuation

articles.title: ČEZ outlines USD392 million plant modernisation plans
articles.summary: Czech nuclear power operator ČEZ has set out its modernisation and investment plans for 2026 at the Dukovany and Temelin nuclear power plants.

articles.title: Sweden proposes steps to facilitate new nuclear projects
articles.summary: The Swedish government has announced several proposed measures to make it easier to establish new nuclear power in the country. These include a new approval law, more possible locations for nuclear power on the coast, and increased government support for municipalities' feasibility studies.

articles.title: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission launches reorganisation
articles.summary: The US nuclear regulator is aiming to implement a reorganisation which it says will streamline decision-making, consolidate functions, and align with national goals for more efficient licensing and deployment of nuclear technology by the end of September.

articles.title: TRISO fuel progress for US reactor pilot programme
articles.summary: BWX Technologies says its TRISO nuclear fuel for Antares Nuclear is on track for "timely completion" for the reactor demonstration planned to meet the US’s 4 July target date.

articles.title: Tepco prepares for restart of Kashiwazaki-Kariwa unit
articles.summary: Japan's Tokyo Electric Power Company plans to restart unit 6 at its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant on Monday. An attempt last month to restart the reactor, which has been offline for almost 14 years, was halted after an alarm was triggered in the control rod operation monitoring system.

articles.title: Tepco restarts Kashiwazaki-Kariwa unit 6
articles.summary: Tokyo Electric Power Company has restarted unit 6 of its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant in Japan's Niigata Prefecture. The company aims to return the reactor to commercial operation on 18 March.

articles.title: Testing of fuel rods taking place for Brazil's microreactor project
articles.summary: Indústrias Nucleares do Brasil is preparing for the final phase of testing for fuel rods to be used in the development of Brazil's national microreactor project.

articles.title: US funding for research into recycling used nuclear fuel
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy's Office of Nuclear Energy has awarded more than USD19 million to five US companies to research and develop recycling technologies for used nuclear fuel.

articles.title: Collaboration on Polish nuclear energy training centre
articles.summary: Orlen Synthos Green Energy has signed an agreement with research and implementation organisation the Łukasiewicz Research Network on broad cooperation in the development of nuclear energy, particularly small modular reactors, in Poland. The agreement includes, among other things, the establishment and joint operation of a nuclear energy training ce

articles.title: Podcast: What should be the target time to build a nuclear plant?
articles.summary: How long should it take from signing a contract to first concrete, to completion, for a new nuclear power plant? And what needs to be done to ensure that funding is unlocked for new units? Those are just two of the topics covered by Assystem's Deputy CEO Stéphane Aubarbier.

articles.title: Domes hoisted at Chinese CAP1000 units
articles.summary: The outer dome of the double-layered containment building of unit 4 of the Haiyang nuclear power plant has been installed, while the inner dome of unit 1 at the Xudabao plant has also been hoisted into place.

articles.title: Copenhagen Atomics reaches pump testing milestone
articles.summary: Danish nuclear technology company Copenhagen Atomics has completed two years of continuous operation of a molten salt pump and test loop at its facilities in Copenhagen. The system has been running without issues under high-temperature molten salt conditions, marking one of the longest continuous durability tests of its kind worldwide, it said. &nb

articles.title: US, Armenia sign agreement on nuclear energy
articles.summary: Days after Rosatom's CEO reiterated the Russian nuclear company's willingness to cooperate with Armenia in the construction of new nuclear capacity, Armenia and the USA have completed negotiations on a cooperation agreement that will pave the way for US companies to strike deals on nuclear power projects in Armenia.

articles.title: Eagles and Newcleo team up for LFR technology demonstrator
articles.summary: The Eagles Consortium has signed a collaboration agreement with France-based innovative reactor developer Newcleo to work together on the realisation of the LEANDREA lead-cooled small modular reactor technology demonstrator at Mol in Belgium.

articles.title: Cold testing of third Sanmen unit completed
articles.summary: Cold functional tests have been completed at unit 3 of the Sanmen nuclear power plant in China's Zhejiang province, China National Nuclear Corporation has announced.

articles.title: India’s Rajasthan unit 7 reaches full power
articles.summary: Rajasthan nuclear power plant’s unit 7 is the third of sixteen 700 MW Indian-designed pressurised heavy water reactors being built in the country.

articles.title: Solstice plans expansion of US conversion facility
articles.summary: Solstice Advanced Materials announced that its Metropolis Works plant in Illinois - the USA's only domestic uranium conversion facility - is expected to produce more than 10,000 tonnes of uranium hexafluoride in 2026, which represents about a 20% increase from its planned output in 2024.

articles.title: EDF to seek approval for new acoustic fish deterrent system
articles.summary: Initial trials show an acoustic fish deterrent system that would use underwater ultrasound technology to keep fish away from Hinkley Point C's water intake system have been effective, EDF has said.

articles.title: Assessment of proposed Norwegian SMR plant to begin
articles.summary: The Norwegian government has given Norsk Kjernekraft approval to begin work on an impact assessment for a nuclear power plant in Aure and Heim municipalities, the first step in the licensing process for nuclear power in Norway.

articles.title: US campaign puts case for disposal, not reprocessing, of used fuel
articles.summary: The Nuclear Scaling Initiative’s Scale What Works campaign says that direct disposal of used nuclear fuel in the US is the "safest, most secure and least expensive pathway for the country" as nuclear energy capacity is expanded.
